skills.name: Contract review issue list
skills.one_liner: Clause-by-clause issues against a playbook, with suggested redlines for attorney review.
skills.description: Reads a contract clause by clause against the owner's playbook, or a conservative default one. It produces an issue list with a business-risk rating, the quoted clause, why it matters in plain English and suggested redline language, plus an obligations and key-dates table. It is a draft for review by a licensed attorney, never a legal opinion.
skills.when: the owner has received a contract, MSA, lease, supplier agreement or terms to sign and wants to know what to push back on before attorney review

inputs.label: The contract and any schedules or referenced documents
Who the counterparty is, what the deal is and what matters most
inputs.example: Payment terms and exclusivity matter most

inputs.label: Governing law and where each party is based
Our preferred, fallback and walk-away positions
When a response or signature is due

outputs.name: Issue list with suggested redlines
outputs.description: Clause ref, quoted text, risk rating, plain-English issue, suggested redline for attorney review, question.

outputs.name: Obligations and key dates
outputs.description: Each obligation, owner, deadline, notice window and renewal date.

outputs.name: Plain-English summary for the owner
outputs.description: The five issues that matter most and questions for the attorney.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Not legal advice.' 2. Record the stated governing law and venue, and flag it if unclear. Every jurisdiction-dependent point is labelled as such. 3. Parse the contract with file_parse (vision_describe for scanned pages) and build a clause map: parties, term and renewal, fees and payment, scope, service levels, IP, confidentiality, data protection, warranties, indemnities, limitation of liability, insurance, termination, assignment, non-solicit and non-compete, dispute resolution, governing law and notices. 4. Load the playbook with memory_recall (preferred, fallback and walk-away positions). If none exists, use a conservative default and say so. 5. For each clause, compare it with the playbook: rate business risk High, Medium or Low, quote the clause, explain the issue in plain English, and propose redline language labelled 'suggested for attorney review'. 6. Flag missing clauses (no liability cap, no termination for convenience) and unusual ones (auto-renewal with a long notice window, unilateral changes, uncapped indemnities, broad IP assignment, most-favoured-customer terms). 7. Extract obligations and key dates (renewal notice windows, payment terms, reporting duties) into the obligations table with spreadsheet_generate. 8. List questions for the attorney and for the counterparty. Never say a clause is enforceable, legal or 'fine'; use cautious language and flag jurisdiction-dependent points. 9. Nothing is sent to the counterparty from this skill. Use request_owner_decision to confirm the attorney review is arranged. 10. State what could not be verified: enforceability in the jurisdiction, referenced documents not provided (schedules, policies, order forms) and uncertainty in scanned text.

workflow.title: Parse contract and map clauses
workflow.brief: Extract text (including scanned pages) and map every clause to its section reference.
workflow.acceptance: Every section appears in the clause map with its reference; governing law recorded or flagged as unclear.

workflow.title: Compare to playbook
workflow.brief: Rate each clause against the playbook and draft suggested redlines.
workflow.acceptance: Each clause has a rating, quoted text, plain-English issue and suggested redline.

workflow.title: Issue list and obligations table
workflow.brief: Render the issue list, obligations table and owner summary.
workflow.acceptance: Every output carries the draft-for-attorney-review label.

workflow.title: Consistency and overstatement check
workflow.brief: Check that nothing reads as a legal conclusion and every High issue has a redline.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; no statement presents a legal conclusion as certain; every High issue has a redline.

workflow.title: Licensed review by an attorney
workflow.brief: The owner's attorney in the relevant jurisdiction reviews the issue list before anything is signed or sent.
workflow.acceptance: Attorney review recorded, or the owner has recorded that review is arranged, before signing or sending.

quality_checks.criterion: Every output is marked as a draft for review by a licensed attorney and not legal advice
Governing law and jurisdiction assumptions are stated
No legal conclusion is stated as certain
Every High-risk issue quotes the clause and proposes redline language for attorney review
Missing standard clauses are flagged
Obligations and notice windows are extracted with dates

skills.name: NDA draft
skills.one_liner: Mutual or one-way NDA drafted from a vetted template for attorney review.
skills.description: Drafts a mutual or one-way NDA from the business's vetted template and the deal facts. It covers the definition of confidential information, standard exclusions, permitted use and disclosure, compelled disclosure, return or destruction, term and remedies. A cover note lists every choice and jurisdiction flag for attorney review before signing.
skills.when: the owner is about to share confidential information with a potential partner, supplier, investor, contractor or buyer

inputs.label: Exact legal names and addresses of both parties
Mutual or one-way, and who discloses
Why information is being shared
Governing law and venue preferred
The business's or counsel's vetted NDA template
Their NDA, if they sent one

outputs.name: NDA draft
outputs.description: Complete NDA marked as a draft for attorney review.

outputs.name: Cover note: choices and questions
outputs.description: Each drafting choice, deviations from template and questions for the attorney.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Not legal advice.' 2. Start from the business's vetted template or counsel's template with memory_recall and embeddings_search. If none exists, use a plain-language standard structure and say clearly that it has not been vetted. 3. Collect the facts: exact legal names and addresses, mutual or one-way, the purpose, governing law and venue, disclosure period and how long confidentiality survives. 4. Draft the core clauses: definition of confidential information (marked and unmarked, with a reasonable-person standard); standard exclusions (public, already known, independently developed, received from a third party); use limited to the purpose; disclosure to representatives with a need to know; compelled disclosure with notice; return or destruction; no licence; no obligation to proceed; remedies including injunctive relief; and, where US law applies, the trade-secret whistleblower immunity notice for the attorney to confirm. 5. Flag choices for the attorney rather than deciding them: term length, residuals clause, non-solicit (often out of place in an NDA), trade-secret survival and jurisdiction-specific points. 6. If the counterparty sent a draft, parse it with file_parse, compare it with the template and list every deviation. 7. Write the cover note listing each choice and open question. 8. This skill never sends or signs. Confirm the attorney review with request_owner_decision. 9. State what could not be verified: enforceability in the chosen jurisdiction and the correctness of entity names.

workflow.brief: Draft the NDA and cover note, and compare against any counterparty draft.
workflow.acceptance: Draft includes all core clauses and the draft label; deviations listed.

workflow.title: Template conformance check
workflow.brief: Check the draft against the template and the flagged choices.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; every deviation from the template is listed; the draft label is present.

workflow.title: Licensed review by an attorney
workflow.brief: The owner's attorney reviews the draft before it is sent or signed.
workflow.acceptance: Attorney review recorded before sending or signing.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Understand the model from the site (web_fetch, and vision_describe on checkout screenshots the owner shares) and from the owner: B2C or B2B, goods, services or digital, subscriptions, accounts, user-generated content, marketplace, age limits. 3. skills.name: Privacy notice draft
skills.one_liner: GDPR/CCPA-aware privacy notice from an actual data map, for review.
skills.description: Drafts a privacy notice aware of GDPR, UK GDPR and CCPA/CPRA, written from the business's actual data map and a check of what the live site collects. It covers what is collected, why, lawful basis, sharing, retention, transfers, rights and contacts, in layered plain language, for review by a privacy professional or counsel.
skills.when: the site or app collects personal data and the notice is missing, copied from a template, or out of date after adding new tools

inputs.label: The business's data map or ROPA
Website or app to check
Where customers and users are
Tools and processors in use
The current notice
Who handles privacy requests

outputs.name: Privacy notice draft
outputs.description: Layered notice: short summary, then full sections, marked as a draft for review.

outputs.name: Mismatch and decisions list
outputs.description: Differences between the data map and the live site, and decisions for counsel.

outputs.name: HTML version for after review
outputs.description: Accessible HTML of the notice, to publish only after review.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (privacy): Data-protection drafts only; minimize personal data; never collect or compile personal data beyond the business purpose. Escalate to a privacy professional or counsel (licensed professional) before anything is published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a privacy professional or counsel.' 2. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Legal interpretations (lawful basis, 'sale' or 'share', transfer mechanisms) are decided by counsel, not by this draft. 3. Start from the data map with memory_recall (run data-map-ropa first if there is none): categories of data, sources, purposes, lawful bases (GDPR Art. 6, and Art. 9 for special categories), recipients and processors, transfers and safeguards, retention. 4. Check the live site with the companion browser: forms, cookies and third-party scripts on key pages. Observe only; submit nothing. Reconcile with the data map and list mismatches, because the notice must describe reality. 5. Draft a layered notice: a short summary, then full sections covering GDPR Art. 13/14 information, CCPA/CPRA disclosures where applicable (categories, sale or share, sensitive information, rights, opt-out links), children, security in general terms, changes and contact. 6. Use plain language (reading age about 12–14) and no catch-alls such as 'we may share with partners'. Do not describe processing the business doesn't do. 7. Minimise: the notice contains no personal data beyond the business contact point. 8. List decisions for counsel: lawful-basis choices, the sale or share determination, the cookie consent mechanism and the transfer mechanism. 9. Render the HTML version with web_page_generate for publication after review only. 10. State what could not be verified: processors' own practices, trackers that load only after consent, and markets not analysed.

workflow.acceptance: Reviewer decisions recorded before publication.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (privacy): Data-protection drafts only; minimize personal data; never collect or compile personal data beyond the business purpose. Escalate to a privacy professional or counsel (licensed professional) before anything is published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a privacy professional or counsel.' 2. Discover systems: apps visible through connectors, billing and vendor lists, and an owner interview covering sales, marketing, support, HR, finance, the website, devices and paper records. 3. For each system record metadata only (field names, data categories, record counts where available) with connector_read. Never export actual personal records. 4. Each item is rated Met, Partial or Missing with a suggested ask, for review by a privacy professional or counsel.

outputs.name: Decision summary

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (privacy): Data-protection drafts only; minimize personal data; never collect or compile personal data beyond the business purpose. Escalate to a privacy professional or counsel (licensed professional) before anything is published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a privacy professional or counsel.' 2. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Contract interpretation and whether terms are adequate are decided by counsel; this skill rates items against a checklist only. 3. Establish context with memory_recall: what personal data the vendor will process, volume, sensitivity and where it will be processed. 4. Parse the DPA and linked documents (sub-processor list, security annex, standard contractual clauses) with file_parse. 5. Check the Article 28(3) elements: documented instructions, confidentiality of personnel, Article 32 security measures, sub-processor authorisation and flow-down, help with data-subject rights and DPIAs, deletion or return at the end, and audit and information rights. Also check breach-notification timing, the international transfer mechanism (SCCs, UK IDTA or addendum, adequacy), liability, and US service-provider or contractor terms where relevant. 6. Security terms: note the certifications claimed (for example SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001) and verify them against the public trust page with web_fetch. Say plainly that the reports themselves were not reviewed unless they were provided. Check encryption, access control, MFA, testing and incident response. Items needing a security judgement go to a qualified security professional. 7. Rate each item Met, Partial, Missing or Not applicable, with the clause reference, and write a suggested ask for each Partial or Missing item (for example 'breach notice within 48 hours'). 8. Summarise the decision: acceptable as is, acceptable with asks, or escalate. 9. State what could not be verified: vendor claims without evidence and the terms of sub-processors.

skills.name: Trademark clearance prep
skills.one_liner: Knockout search across public databases and a memo for attorney review.
skills.description: Runs a knockout trademark search for a proposed name or logo across public registers (USPTO, EUIPO, WIPO Global Brand Database, UKIPO and others as relevant) and common-law web use, domains and handles, organised by Nice class. It produces a memo with hits graded on likelihood-of-confusion factors, for attorney review. It is never a clearance opinion.
skills.when: before paying for a logo, printing packaging, registering a domain or launching under a new name

inputs.label: The name, tagline or logo
What will be sold under it
inputs.example: Baked goods, jarred preserves, online and in store

inputs.label: Where it will be used
The logo, if any

outputs.name: Knockout search memo
outputs.description: Summary, registers searched with queries and dates, hits table, risk grading, alternatives and questions for the attorney.

outputs.name: Hits table
outputs.description: Mark, owner, status, classes, goods, filing date, link and risk grade.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed trademark attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before adoption, filing or spend, and mark the memo 'Knockout search for attorney review. Not a clearance opinion.' 2. Describe the goods and services and map them to likely Nice classes, plus coordinated classes. 3. Search the relevant registers through the companion browser (search forms only; nothing is filed or submitted): USPTO trademark search, EUIPO eSearch or TMview, WIPO Global Brand Database, UKIPO and national registers for target markets. Cover identical marks, phonetic equivalents, spelling variants and translations; compare design marks with vision_describe. 4. Search common-law use with web_search and web_fetch: the web, marketplaces, business registries, domain availability and social handles. 5. Record each hit: mark, owner, status (live or dead), classes, goods, filing date and link. 6. Grade each hit low, medium or high using likelihood-of-confusion factors (similarity in sight, sound and meaning; relatedness of goods; trade channels) as input for the attorney, not a conclusion. 7. Note distinctiveness concerns (descriptive or generic words) and suggest alternatives to test. 8. Write the memo with registers, queries, dates, the hits table and questions for the attorney. 9. State what could not be verified: registers not searched, unregistered offline use and pending applications not yet published.

workflow.title: Goods, services and classes
workflow.brief: Describe goods and services and map to Nice classes with reasons.
workflow.acceptance: Classes listed with reasons.

workflow.title: Register searches
workflow.brief: Search each register for identical, phonetic, variant and translated marks, and design marks.
workflow.acceptance: Each register searched with query strings, date and result counts logged; screenshots of key hits; nothing submitted beyond search.

workflow.title: Common-law, domain and handle checks
workflow.brief: Search web use, marketplaces, registries, domains and handles.
workflow.acceptance: Each check has a link and date.

workflow.title: Grade hits
workflow.brief: Grade each hit on likelihood-of-confusion factors.
workflow.acceptance: Every hit has a grade with the factors behind it.

workflow.title: Knockout memo
workflow.brief: Write the memo and hits table.
workflow.acceptance: Memo carries the not-a-clearance-opinion label.

workflow.title: Licensed review by a trademark attorney
workflow.brief: A trademark attorney reviews the memo before adoption or filing.
workflow.acceptance: Attorney review recorded before adoption or spend.

quality_checks.criterion: Marked as knockout research for review by a licensed attorney, not a clearance opinion
Every register searched is listed with its queries and date
No conclusion that a mark is available or safe to use
Phonetic, spelling and translation variants are searched
Nice classes are mapped with reasons

skills.example_request: We want to rename the bakery 'Little Ember Bakehouse' and start selling jars online nationally. Is anyone already using that name before I pay a designer?

skills.name: Company policy draft
skills.one_liner: A clear policy with scope, rules, exceptions and owner, for qualified review.
skills.description: Drafts a clear company policy (purpose, scope, definitions, rules, exceptions and who approves them, roles, enforcement, review date) in plain language. It is benchmarked against primary-source guidance and flagged by jurisdiction, with a staff summary, for review by an attorney, or by employment counsel where staff are affected.
skills.when: the business needs a rule written down: expenses, company cards, remote work, device use, refunds, gifts, conflicts of interest, data retention or similar

inputs.label: What the policy covers and why now
inputs.example: Expenses and company cards; people keep buying lunches

inputs.label: Where staff and operations are
What happens today
Existing policies and handbook

outputs.name: Policy draft
outputs.description: Standard structure with owner, version and review date, marked as a draft for qualified review.

outputs.name: Staff summary
outputs.description: One page: what changes, what to do, who to ask.

outputs.name: Jurisdiction flags and sources
outputs.description: Requirements that vary by place, with primary-source links.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Not legal advice.' 2. Guardrail (employment_law): Policies and processes as drafts with jurisdiction flags. Terminations, discipline, accommodations, classification and pay-equity questions escalate to the owner and counsel. Where the policy affects staff, escalate to employment counsel or a qualified HR professional (licensed professional); the policy never decides an individual case. 3. Clarify the problem the policy solves and who it applies to; check existing policies with embeddings_search and file_parse for conflicts. 4. Research requirements and reputable guidance from primary sources (regulators, government guidance, standards bodies) for each jurisdiction with web_search and web_fetch, and flag where the rules differ by state or country. 5. Draft in a standard structure: purpose, scope, definitions, policy statements (must and must not), procedures, exceptions and who approves them, roles and responsibilities, related documents, enforcement, and review cadence with version and owner. 6. Write in plain language: short sentences, 'you' and 'we', and examples for grey areas. 7. Flag employment-related items (discipline, leave, monitoring, accommodations, pay deductions) for employment counsel. 8. Add an acknowledgement line and a one-page staff summary; confirm policy choices with the owner via request_owner_decision. 9. State what could not be verified: jurisdictional variations not researched, and practices the owner described but that aren't documented.

workflow.title: Requirements and guidance
workflow.brief: Research requirements and guidance per jurisdiction from primary sources.
workflow.acceptance: Every requirement cites a primary source and jurisdiction.

workflow.title: Draft the policy
workflow.brief: Draft the policy, staff summary and flag list.
workflow.acceptance: Standard structure complete; draft label present.

workflow.title: Plain-language and conflict review
workflow.brief: Check readability and conflicts with existing policies.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; no conflict with existing policies remains unflagged.

workflow.title: Licensed review by an attorney or employment counsel
workflow.brief: An attorney, or employment counsel or a qualified HR professional where staff are affected, reviews before adoption.
workflow.acceptance: Qualified reviewer recorded before adoption.

quality_checks.criterion: Marked as a draft for review by an attorney, or by employment counsel or a qualified HR professional where staff are affected
Jurisdiction flags accompany every requirement that varies by place
No individual employment decision is made or implied
No legal conclusion is stated as certain
Standard structure with owner and review date
Plain-language reading level

skills.example_request: We need a proper expense and company-card policy. People keep buying lunches on the card and I don't know what's allowed. Draft something fair.

skills.name: Regulatory requirements research
skills.one_liner: Requirements from primary sources for a business activity and place, with citations.
skills.description: Researches the licences, permits, registrations and rules that apply to a specific activity in a specific place, from primary sources, at every layer of jurisdiction. Output is a requirements matrix (citation, agency, conditions, deadlines, published fees, effective dates), a sequenced path, and questions for the attorney and the agency.
skills.when: the owner plans a new activity, product, location or market and needs to know what rules apply before spending money

inputs.label: The activity in concrete terms
inputs.example: Selling homemade hot sauce at farmers markets and online

inputs.label: Where, down to city or county
Entity type, size and current licences
When the owner wants to start

outputs.name: Requirements matrix
outputs.description: Requirement, citation and link, agency, applies-when, deadline, fee as published, effective and last-updated dates, penalty, evidence.

outputs.name: Regulatory research memo
outputs.description: Summary, sequenced path, open questions and pending changes.

outputs.name: Permit sequence
outputs.description: What must happen before what.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Not legal advice.' 2. Define the activity precisely and every layer of jurisdiction: federal or national, state or province, county, city and sector regulators. 3. Search primary sources only for requirements with web_search and web_fetch: statutes, regulations, agency guidance and official forms. Use secondary sources only to find primary ones. Use the companion browser for agency portals and lookups that need filters, and submit nothing. 4. For each requirement capture: the requirement, citation and link, agency, conditions that trigger it, deadlines, fees as published, effective date and last-updated date, penalty and evidence required. 5. Note conflicts, ambiguities and pending changes (proposed rules, consultations). 6. Build the requirements matrix and a sequenced path with diagram_generate (for example zoning before building permit before health permit). 7. List questions for the attorney and for the agency. 8. Offer watch-a-page on key agency pages so changes are caught. 9. State what could not be verified: local rules not published online, interpretive questions and pages without a last-updated date.

workflow.title: Primary-source search
workflow.brief: Search every jurisdiction layer for requirements from primary sources.
workflow.acceptance: Every requirement has a primary-source link and date.

workflow.title: Agency portal lookups
workflow.brief: Use agency portals that need filters or lookups; submit nothing.
workflow.acceptance: Lookup pages recorded with URLs; nothing submitted.

workflow.title: Requirements matrix and sequence
workflow.brief: Build the matrix and the dependency sequence.
workflow.acceptance: Each requirement is placed in sequence with its dependencies.

workflow.title: Citation audit
workflow.brief: Check each citation supports its requirement and is current.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; every requirement cites a primary source; outdated pages flagged.

workflow.title: Licensed review by an attorney
workflow.brief: The owner's attorney reviews interpretations before the owner acts or spends.
workflow.acceptance: Attorney review recorded or marked as pending before action.

quality_checks.criterion: Every requirement cites a primary source with a link and date
Marked as research for review by a licensed attorney; no conclusion is stated as certain
Jurisdiction layers are listed explicitly
Pending changes are flagged
A sequenced path with dependencies is included

skills.example_request: I want to sell homemade hot sauce at farmers markets and online in Oregon. What licences and rules apply? Give me the actual sources.

skills.name: Clause library & playbook
skills.one_liner: Preferred, fallback and walk-away positions for common clauses.
skills.description: Builds a contract playbook from the business's own signed contracts and templates. For each common clause it gives preferred, fallback and walk-away positions with plain-English reasons, approved language, and who may approve deviations. It is drafted for attorney approval, then saved so reviews and negotiations stay fast and consistent.
skills.when: the business negotiates similar contracts repeatedly and argues about the same clauses each time

inputs.label: Signed contracts and templates
inputs.example: The last 20 client agreements in Dropbox

inputs.label: What the owner will and won't accept
The kinds of contracts in scope
inputs.example: Client services agreements and supplier terms

inputs.label: Positions or templates from counsel

outputs.name: Clause playbook
outputs.description: Per clause: preferred, fallback and walk-away positions, rationale, approved language, approver.

outputs.name: Position matrix
outputs.description: Clause types against what the business has actually agreed, with ranges and outliers.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Not legal advice.' 2. Collect signed contracts and templates with file_parse, and extract clauses by type with embeddings_search: limitation of liability, indemnity, IP, confidentiality, payment, term and renewal, termination, warranties, service levels, data protection, governing law, assignment and non-solicit. 3. For each clause type, show in code_interpreter what the business has actually agreed to (the range across contracts and the outliers) and where it has been burned. 4. Propose positions: preferred (our paper), one or two fallbacks (acceptable concessions) and walk-away (escalate or decline), each with a plain-English rationale and a business-risk rating. 5. Attach approved language to each position, taken from the business's vetted templates or counsel. Mark any new language 'proposed for attorney drafting', never vetted. 6. Set approval rules: who may accept fallback positions (owner, counsel), and a deviation log. 7. Ask the owner to set risk appetite on each walk-away point with request_owner_decision. 8. After attorney approval, propose saving the library with memory_write for contract-issue-list and negotiation-prep. 9. State what could not be verified: enforceability of positions by jurisdiction and contracts not provided.

workflow.title: Extract clauses from past contracts
workflow.brief: Parse contracts and tag clauses by type.
workflow.acceptance: Every contract is parsed; each clause type has its examples listed.

workflow.title: Current-position analysis
workflow.brief: Summarise ranges and outliers per clause type.
workflow.acceptance: Each clause type shows range, outliers and count.

workflow.title: Draft the playbook
workflow.brief: Draft positions, rationales, language and approvers.
workflow.acceptance: Every position has a rationale and approver; new language is labelled proposed.

workflow.title: Owner sets risk appetite
workflow.brief: The owner confirms walk-away points and approval rules.
workflow.acceptance: Owner decisions recorded per clause type.

workflow.title: Licensed review by an attorney
workflow.brief: The owner's attorney approves the positions and language.
workflow.acceptance: Attorney approval recorded before the library is used.

workflow.title: Save the approved library
workflow.brief: Propose the approved library as shared memory.
workflow.acceptance: Memory proposal cites the playbook version and approval date.

quality_checks.criterion: Marked as a draft for approval by a licensed attorney
Every position has a plain-English rationale and a named approver
New language is labelled proposed, never presented as vetted
Shows the range the business has actually agreed to
Walk-away positions are explicit

skills.example_request: Every time a client sends their contract we argue about the same five clauses. Can you build us a playbook of what we accept and what we don't, so I stop reinventing it?

skills.name: Dispute letter draft
skills.one_liner: A firm, factual letter draft for a dispute, for attorney review before sending.
skills.description: Drafts a firm, factual letter for a dispute: a dated chronology with an evidence index, the terms relied on, the remedy and amount with its calculation, a reasonable deadline and next steps the owner is prepared to take. It comes in softer and firmer variants, with no threats, defamation or admissions, for attorney review before sending.
skills.when: a customer, supplier, contractor or landlord has not done what was agreed and conversation has not fixed it

inputs.label: What happened, in the owner's words
inputs.example: Contractor took a $9,000 deposit and hasn't shown up in six weeks

inputs.label: Contract, invoices, emails, messages and photos
What the owner wants and the minimum acceptable
inputs.example: Full deposit back, or a start date within 14 days

inputs.label: Who they are and their address
Where each party is and where the work happened

outputs.name: Dispute letter draft (softer and firmer variants)
outputs.description: Marked as a draft for attorney review before sending.

outputs.name: Chronology and evidence index
outputs.description: Date, event, evidence reference and source file.

skills.instructions: 1. Guardrail (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed professional) before anything is signed, sent, published or relied on, and mark every output 'DRAFT for review by a licensed attorney. Not legal advice.' 2. Build a dated chronology from the documents (contracts, invoices, emails, messages, photos read with vision_describe) with an evidence index. Quote the exact terms relied on. 3. Clarify the owner's goal (payment, repair, refund, stopping an action) and minimum acceptable outcome, and consider whether a call or mediation should come first. 4. Draft the letter: the facts in neutral language; the obligation and how it was not met, with references; the specific remedy and amount with its calculation; a reasonable deadline; and the next step if unresolved (for example mediation or small claims), but only steps the owner is actually prepared to take. 5. Avoid defamatory statements, admissions, emotional language, and threats of criminal prosecution or regulatory complaints used as leverage. 6. Flag jurisdiction points for the attorney: limitation periods, pre-action requirements (such as letter-before-claim protocols), consumer-law rules and 'without prejudice' usage. 7. Provide a softer and a firmer variant; confirm the chosen tone and remedy with request_owner_decision. 8. This skill never sends the letter. 9. State what could not be verified: facts from the owner's account without documents, and the counterparty's position.

workflow.title: Evidence and chronology
workflow.brief: Parse the documents and build the chronology and evidence index.
workflow.acceptance: Every event has a date and an evidence reference, or is marked owner-reported.

workflow.title: Draft letter variants
workflow.brief: Draft the softer and firmer variants.
workflow.acceptance: Both variants state facts, terms, remedy with calculation and deadline; draft label present.

workflow.title: Tone and risk review
workflow.brief: Check for threats, defamation, admissions and unsupported claims.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; no threats, defamatory statements or unsupported claims; every fact cites the evidence index.

workflow.title: Licensed review by an attorney
workflow.brief: The owner's attorney reviews the letter before anything is sent.
workflow.acceptance: Attorney review recorded before sending.

quality_checks.criterion: Marked as a draft for review by a licensed attorney before sending
Every factual statement is tied to evidence
No threats of criminal action, defamatory language or admissions
Jurisdiction points such as limitation periods and pre-action rules are flagged, not decided
The remedy amount shows its calculation
Softer and firmer variants are offered

skills.example_request: A contractor took a $9,000 deposit for our shop fit-out and hasn't shown up in six weeks. I want a firm letter demanding the money back, for my lawyer to check first.
